proof_decision.trust_question: After a module operation refreshes facts, does a discarded runtime snapshot and fresh public-provider discovery expose exactly the owner-backed revision, stale state, or removal while committed payload mirrors remain source-aligned?
proof_decision.narrowest_evidence: The module contract and scenario matrices execute elevated@r1 through refresh, discard the prior discovered/runtime packet, and freshly resolve clear@r2, stale@r3, and removal@r4 for both start and implement; focused negatives retain omission, undeclared-fact, irrelevant-module, collision, and non-reconciling-owner coverage. Strict payload validation separately proves the committed source/payload/root-install boundary is current.
proof_decision.prune_or_replacement_condition: Replace only when contract-owned conformance proves the same operation-to-owner-to-fresh-discovery transition and all negative states through both ordinary consumers, while the strict committed-payload alignment guard remains authoritative.
proof_decision.residual_risk: A module owner remains responsible for making its provider snapshot durable enough for its own process and storage model; Workspace now rejects a reported fact snapshot unless an immediate fresh provider read agrees, but cannot supply module-domain persistence itself.
